full_judgment: 4. The kabala was to be registered by 17th January, 1961 but as the defendants were dilly dallying the execution of the kabala the plaintiff served a legal notice on 8.1.61. The defendant 3 promptly executed the kabala in. so far as 1/3rd share is concerned on 27.1.81. When 3 persons stipulate that they agree to sell their properties. it is obvious that the tenor of such agreement is that they held it in equal shares, The presumption is rebuttable no doubt. But that has not happened in this case. If the High Court Division had approached the contract from the correct perspective then it would have held otherwise as to, the quantum of the share of each individual contracted. The subsequent kabala by the defendant No. 3 re-enforces the view that each one of them was holding equal share in the property namely 1/3rd share. No evidence was laid that the nature of the property is such that the purchaser would be bereft of the enjoyment of the property if by running a blue pencil the contract was made divisible and enforced by specific performance for contract Here the purchaser has sought specific performance. The property in question is .153 acres of land with structures, etc. On the other hand, the parties themselves treated it as a divisible contract and the kabala dated 27.1.61 proves the point.
